newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI won't comment on Lonrho report.
newsitem.headline: JCI won't comment on Lonrho report.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd on Tuesday declined to comment on news reports it could decide within days on whether to go ahead with a proposed merger with British conglomerate Lonrho Plc.
"We have no comment on the JCI/Lonrho story from London," JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves told Reuters.
London's Financial Times earlier on Tuesday quoted Lonrho Plc chief executive Nick Morrell saying, "I believe the position with JCI will be clarified in days, rather than weeks."
Lonrho said on Monday that merger talks with JCI Ltd were continuing, but added the negotiations were still at an early stage.
Lonrho also said it had no plans to divest its stake in Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd at this point.
The comment followed a press report in London over the weekend that the Ashanti holding was being sized up by South Africa's Gencor Ltd.
Lonrho and JCI said in May they were holding preliminary negotiations.
Press reports at the time said both companies were looking for a merger deal under which Lonrho's stake in Ashanti would go to Anglo American Corp of South Africa.
In return, Anglo's 28 percent stake in Lonrho would be bought back and cancelled by the British mining-to-hotels conglomerate.
But asked whether Lonrho was seeking to divest its 41 percent holding in Ghana's Ashanti, Morrell said: "Ashanti is a very important asset and we have no plans at this stage to divest it."
